info.desc: Sandinista! is the fourth studio album by the punk rock band The Clash. It was released in 1980 as a triple album containing 36 tracks, with 6 songs on each side. Anticipating the "world music" trend of the 1980s, it features reggae, jazz, mock gospel, rockabilly, folk, dub, rhythm and blues, calypso, and rap. For the first time, the band's traditional songwriting credits of Strummer/Jones were replaced by a generic credit to "The Clash",and the band cut the album royalties, in order to release the 3-LP at a low price. The title comes from the Nicaraguan left-wing guerrilla organization, the .

podcast.body: Released on December 12, 1980, just 363 days after *London Calling*, this was a sprawling and sometimes messy triple album. Its title reflects the band's solidarity with the Sandinista Communist Rebels who overthrew the government in Nicaragua in 1979. To get CBS to agree to release a triple album, The Clash made significant financial concessions, foregoing any royalties on the first 200,000 copies, a risky move as *London Calling* had only sold 180,000 copies at that point. The album incorporated an even wider array of influences, including gospel music and children's choirs, in an attempt to display vision, though some felt it became self-indulgent and that not all 36 songs sounded finished.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The song "The Magnificent Seven" was recorded in March 1980 at Electric Lady Studios specifically for this album. "It's a song by the clash that they recorded at an electric lady in March of 1980 for the Sandinista album."

podcast.body: The triple album *Sandinista!*, released by The Clash in 1980, included a song called "Charlie Don't Surf" which featured surfing elements in its arrangement. "In 1980, the clash released their Sandinista album, a triple record that contained a song based on a line from Apocalypse Now."
